stories.title: Ukraine claims strikes on two Russian boats off Libya
summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday said Ukraine was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, adding that one of them sank in the latest spillover from Moscow’s war with Kyiv.

But the United Nations condemned the strikes, warning against the prospect of a country still divided after the Libyan civil war becoming “a battleground for foreign conflicts”. “It all took place off the coast of Libya.

stories.title: In meeting with Dar, Portuguese foreign minister reaffirms commitment to bolstering Islamabad-Lisbon ties
summary: Portuguese Minister of State and Foreign Affairs Paulo Rangel reaffirmed on Monday his country’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations with Pakistan, a statement by the Foreign Office (FO) said.
In today’s meeting, Rangel and Dar reviewed the “longstanding and friendly relations between Pakistan and Portugal as the two countries mark 77 years of diplomatic relations”, the FO statement said.

Moreover, Rangel appreciated Pakistan’s “constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability”, the statement said, adding that the two leaders also emphasised the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and effective multilateralism in addressing shared challenges.

stories.title: Asif says process for referendum on new provinces likely to move forward early next year
summary: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has said discussions on a possible referendum to create new provinces are expected to take a “definitive shape” by the end of this year, with the process likely to move forward early next year.

Asked whether the PML-N and the federal government had reached a principled decision on holding a referendum, and what its timeline and outline would be, he said: “Perhaps by the year-end, all this debate and discussion that is taking place will take some definitive shape.
The federal government, however, maintains that a referendum is a legal and constitutional means of gauging public opinion on the creation of new provinces.

stories.title: ADB invests in Pakistan-based B2B fintech company Neem
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Monday said it invested an undisclosed amount in Neem, a Pakistan-based B2B fintech company that helps businesses receive, manage, and pay out money digitally.

Pakistan has made strong progress in digitising consumer payments, with the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP)’s instant payment system, Raast, and mobile wallets bringing millions of people onto digital rails.

Neem’s solutions are built to meet the payment needs of businesses of every size, including women-owned businesses and micro-entrepreneurs, so access to modern financial infrastructure is not limited to large enterprises.

stories.title: Bad COP, worse COP: What’s next after climate talks fail?
summary: The “conference of the parties” talks, better known as COP31, ended without agreement and two days over schedule on Sunday, as countries deadlocked on fossil fuels, finance, science and carbon-removing technologies.
As a result, few suggest the process should be abandoned, but there are growing calls for alternatives to advance climate change action, including legal suits.
Others expect growing interest in agreements made outside the COP process, like the Santa Marta initiative, bringing together countries committed to phasing out fossil fuels.

stories.title: Suspect can be tried under federal law for inter-provincial drug smuggling, rules Peshawar High Court
summary: PESHAWAR: Peshawar High Court has ruled that special courts could conduct trial under the federal anti-narcotics law if an accused has been arrested by Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF) on charges of inter-provincial smuggling, otherwise, the provincial law will be applicable.

stories.title: KP governor invites investment in renewable energy sector

During the visit, exhibition head Khwaja Wahaj briefed the governor on the latest solar technologies and various products showcased by participating companies.

The governor appreciated the participation of national and international companies, describing the exhibition as an important platform for promoting renewable energy, modern solar solutions and investment opportunities in the province.

stories.title: Netanyahu and Eisenkot’s parties resume talks to form coalition govt in Israel
summary: HERZLIYA: The parties of caretaker Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot launched a new round of talks on Sunday over whether to form a coalition government, with Netanyahu’s party insisting on keeping his main policies.

His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra-Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud.

A minority Eisenkot government could receive support from the 19 Ar­­­­ab party lawmakers but Eisen­kot’s right-wing ally Avigdor Liber­man rejects working with them and instead advocates an alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties.

summary: World number two Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand captured her third consecutive LPGA Tour Championship on Sunday, holding off Japan's Aki Iwai to become the tour's all-time prize money leader.

Iwai, whose only LPGA title came last year at Portland, had a third chance to match Jeeno for the lead but lipped out on a five-foot birdie putt at the par-five 17th.
